subject: Finova — Performance SLOs & Regional Routing (post-demo)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Peter Lang <peter.lang@finova.com>
Cc: nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com, aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2026 15:15:00 -0700
Subject: Finova — Performance SLOs & Regional Routing (post-demo)

Hi Peter / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good conversation and appreciate the clear framing of the platform constraints. Recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can align on a scoped POC.

Key items we captured: 
- Latency targets (p95) you mentioned as a target envelope: US ~120–200ms, EU ~140–220ms, APAC ~200–300ms (end-to-end generation for short prompts). Please confirm target percentiles (p50/p95/p99) that matter most.
- Throughput & concurrency: you called out ~2k–3k requests/minute for peak batch windows and sustained concurrency of 40–100 simultaneous sessions.
- Streaming: streaming responses required for chat flows (token-by-token streaming). You indicated a hard requirement for sub-200ms first-byte for interactive flows.
- Regional routing/data residency: traffic should preferably stay in-region. EU customer data must remain in EU for storage/kv-cache; APAC must prefer SG/TK regions.

Attached is an initial SLO matrix (SLO_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a short template for network traces we can use. Can you confirm the numbers above (p95 latency, throughput, concurrency) and the acceptable fallback SLOs if we need to route to a nearby region during capacity events? Also please share any existing network egress constraints or IP allow-lists we need to plan for.

Next steps we propose:
1) Tech deep-dive (45–60m) this week to validate request/response sizes, average token length, and streaming requirements (we'll include our infra lead, Nikhil, and solutions engineer, Aditya).
2) Provide sample traffic profile + 24–72h traces from your environment (network traces attached if you have them).
3) Agree on POC success criteria and a staged rollout plan: single-region POC -> multi-region routing test -> canary SLA.

Thanks — happy to slot the deep-dive; what times work for your platform team?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: SLO_matrix_v2.xlsx]

From: Peter Lang <peter.lang@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Sinha <priya.sinha@finova.com>, Finova Network Team <netops@finova.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finova — Performance SLOs & Regional Routing (post-demo)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear notes and the matrix — helpful. Confirming the immediate targets from our side (these are for the initial POC; we can tighten after a baseline):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation target = 200ms (US), 220ms (EU), 300ms (APAC). p50 targets are ~70–120ms depending on region. p99 we're tracking but expect higher variance.
- Throughput: spike capacity ~3,000 requests/min (50 requests/sec peak bursts), sustained ~1,200–1,800 rpm depending on time-of-day.
- Concurrency: expected 60–80 active concurrent user sessions for month 1, grow to 150 in Q4.
- Streaming: yes, streaming is required for chat; first-byte <=200ms for interactive sessions is a hard requirement for our UX.
- Data residency: EU customer data must be stored and have KV/cache residency in EU (no cross-region replication of persistent customer data). For APAC we prefer Singapore (ap-southeast-1); Tokyo acceptable if latency better.

We've attached a short network trace from a recent load test (network-trace-example.txt). For the POC we can provide a 72-hour sample and some representative payloads (avg tokens per request ~120, median ~45).

One note on fallback: we can accept routing to a neighboring region for short windows (max 30m) during capacity events, but we need a documented fallback policy and a way to notify/stall sessions if routing causes data residency concerns.

Availability for the deep-dive: Tue/Wed this week 10–14 PST. Who will join from your infra team?

Regards,
Peter Lang
Head of Platform | Finova
plang@finova.com
[Attachment: network-trace-example.txt]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Peter Lang <peter.lang@finova.com>
Cc: nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com, aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finova — Performance SLOs & Regional Routing (post-demo)

Great — thanks for the confirmation and the trace, Peter. Quick notes and proposed agenda for the deep-dive: 

Agenda (45–60m):
- Quick review of traffic profile & sample payloads (you) — confirm avg/median tokens and streaming semantics.
- Inference topology options (Redwood): single-region pinned model vs multi-region active/active with smart routing.
- Caching & KV residency: how we keep per-customer KV in-region and options for cache warmers.
- Batching/throughput tuning: expected batching gains at your payload sizes & estimated tokens/sec.
- Fallback & monitoring: automated fallback policies, notification hooks, and SLO rollback thresholds.

Action items we’ll take:
- Nikhil will run a quick internal validation on cross-region KV constraints and feasible cache partitioning strategies.
- Aditya will prepare an initial throughput/latency projection using your sample payload sizes and target concurrency.
- I'll prepare a POC proposal (timeline: kickoff within 2 weeks, 2–4 week single-region POC, then multi-region test) and a draft success criteria doc.

Proposed slots: Tue 6 Jul 10:30–11:15 PST or Wed 7 Jul 11:00–12:00 PST. Please pick one and we'll send a calendar invite with a short pre-reads link.

Also sharing a HubSpot link and a Drive folder with our SLO templates and a sample routing config for your network/security team.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa

[Links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/Finova, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-SLOs]

From: nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Finova POC — immediate tech checks

Marissa / Aditya — quick internal note after reading their traces and the targets: 
- We'll validate whether p95=200ms (US) is achievable with their avg token sizes given streaming requirement. Likely needs aggressive batching + KV warm cache.
- Need to confirm if the KV/cache shape is per-customer or per-region; if we have to guarantee EU-resident KV, we'll partition caches and ensure no cross-region replication. That will affect warm-up times.
- Quantization/FP16 impact: if they require larger models, check latency impact on APAC nodes.
- Action: Aditya, run the throughput projection (use token med=45, avg=120) and share numbers by EOD. I'll draft a proposed cache partition approach and a minimal fallback policy that preserves residency for storage.

Thanks,
Nikhil
Lead Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com
